Jonathan and David
JON-uh-thuhn and DAY-vid
proper nouns (Old Testament figures)
Jonathan (Hebrew Yehonathan) means "the LORD has given," the eldest son of King Saul; David (Hebrew Dawid) means "beloved," the son of Jesse anointed king over Israel.

Biblical Definition

Jonathan the son of Saul and David the son of Jesse are joined in Scripture as the pattern of covenant friendship, recorded in First Samuel chapters eighteen through twenty. When David had slain Goliath, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and he loved him as his own soul; and Jonathan made a covenant with David, stripping himself of his robe and his garments, even his sword and his bow and his girdle, and giving them to the LORD's anointed. Here is self-denying love at its highest pitch among men, for Jonathan was heir to the throne, yet he willingly preferred the man God had chosen above himself, saying, Thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee. He warned David of his father's murderous designs, interceded for him, and bound their houses in a covenant of loyalty before the LORD. This friendship was not mere natural affection but a bond sealed in the fear of God and in submission to the divine election of David. Jonathan's love, surpassing the love of women, dimly images the love of Christ who lays down His robes and His life for His friends, and the love that ought to bind the saints. Though Jonathan fell in battle, David kept the covenant to his seed in Mephibosheth, showing kindness for Jonathan's sake.

Webster 1828 Definition

The covenant friendship of Saul's son and David, marked by a love that gladly yielded the throne to the LORD's anointed.

JONATHAN AND DAVID, proper nouns. Jonathan, "the LORD has given"; David, "beloved," the anointed king.

The friendship recorded in First Samuel, sealed by a covenant and a token of garments.

A pattern of self-denying loyalty, the heir preferring the chosen above his own crown.

As it is written, "Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul" (1 Sam 18:3).

A faint image of the love of Christ for His friends and the love that binds the saints.

Key Scripture

1Sa 18:1 — "And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul."

1Sa 18:3 — "Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul."

1Sa 20:17 — "And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul."

1Sa 20:42 — "And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the LORD, saying, The LORD be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city."

Modern Corruption

Modern voices sometimes distort this covenant friendship into a romantic or sexual reading, against the plain witness of the text.

expand to see more

Recent attempts to sexualize the friendship of Jonathan and David impose an alien category upon a chaste and holy bond. The text speaks of a love knit in soul and sealed by covenant before the LORD, the love of brothers in arms and saints in faith. To recast it as an erotic relationship not only contradicts the express moral law of God, which everywhere condemns such union, but also robs Scripture of its true and higher meaning. David's lament that Jonathan's love was wonderful, passing the love of women, exalts the purity and depth of covenant loyalty, not carnal desire.

The principle to recover is the dignity of godly friendship and self-denying love. Jonathan, the natural heir, gladly subordinated his ambition to the revealed will of God, preferring David whom the LORD had chosen. Such love—willing to lay down its own glory for another and for the kingdom of God—points beyond itself to the love of the Lord Jesus, who emptied Himself and laid down His life for His friends.

Hebrew Roots

The bond is rooted in submission to God's sovereign choice of David and in the covenant-keeping faith of both men.

expand to see more

David's anointing by Samuel set him apart as the LORD's chosen king (1 Sam 16).

Jonathan's love arose after David's victory over Goliath (1 Sam 18:1).

The covenant was renewed and bound to their seed for ever (1 Sam 20:42).

Saul's jealousy made Jonathan an intercessor and protector for David.

David kept the covenant after Jonathan's death by his kindness to Mephibosheth (2 Sam 9).

Usage

""Knit in soul" describes the deepest godly friendship between believers."

"Jonathan stripping off his robe pictures the surrender of self for the LORD's anointed."

"The covenant "between my seed and thy seed" shows friendship binding even future generations."
